the state of being joined or united or linked
the act of making or becoming a single unit

examples.text: he looked forward to the unification of his family for the holidays

connections.gloss: Use 'unification' when focusing on the creation of unity or oneness, especially in political, organizational, or conceptual contexts.

senses.definition: an unhappy and worried mental state

examples.text: she didn't realize the upset she caused me

connections.gloss: Use 'distress' for a stronger, more formal sense of emotional suffering than 'upset'.

senses.definition: on a floor above

examples.text: they lived upstairs

connections.gloss: Use 'above' when the vertical location is clear from context, especially in homes or buildings, to sound more concise and slightly formal.

senses.definition: The plan was utterly absurd from the start.
completely and without qualification

examples.text: utterly miserable

connections.gloss: Use 'utterly' to intensify a negative or extreme quality, often in emotional or strong judgments.

senses.definition: having great material or monetary value especially for use or exchange

examples.text: a valuable diamond

connections.gloss: Use 'valuable' when something is highly prized or of great worth, often implying deep appreciation or significance.
Use when something is highly valued emotionally or materially, often implying rarity.
Use when something is so valuable that its worth cannot be measured; extremely useful.

senses.definition: something a little different from others of the same type

examples.text: a variant of the same word

senses.definition: an event that departs from expectations
an event that departs from expectations
(biology) a group of organisms within a species that differ in trivial ways from similar groups
a variable quantity that is random

connections.gloss: Use when specifying a different version of the word's sound or spelling, rather than the general form.
Use 'variant' when you want to emphasize a specific version or type of the altered organism, often in a more technical or comparative context.
Use 'deviation' to highlight a measurable or systematic difference from an expected standard; more technical than 'variant' for data or processes.

senses.definition: A small vein, especially one that connects capillaries to a larger vein.

examples.text: Venules and arterioles are small diameter blood vessels that connect capillaries to veins and arteries.

senses.definition: The venules merge into larger veins as they exit the capillary network.
a minute vein continuous with a capillary
the power or right to prohibit or reject a proposed or intended act (especially the power of a chief executive to reject a bill passed by the legislature)

examples.text: On July tenth, the veto was announced.

senses.definition: a vote that blocks a decision
a vote that blocks a decision

connections.gloss: Use when referring to the power to formally reject a decision or proposal, especially in a political or organizational context.

senses.definition: a way of regarding situations or topics etc.

examples.text: consider what follows from the positivist view

connections.gloss: Use 'view' when describing a personal or specific perspective.
Use 'perspective' when emphasizing a particular angle or way of seeing things, often influenced by personal experience or context.
Use 'outlook' when referring to a general attitude or mental tendency toward future events.

senses.definition: She gave a vigorous speech that energized the crowd.
characterized by forceful and energetic action or activity

examples.text: a vigorous hiker

senses.definition: strong and active physically or mentally

examples.text: a vigorous old man who spent half of his day on horseback- W.H.Hudson

connections.gloss: Use 'vigorous' for strong, healthy, and active energy, often physical.

senses.definition: a choice that is made by counting the number of people in favor of each alternative

examples.text: they allowed just one vote per person

connections.gloss: Use 'ballot' instead of 'vote' when referring to the physical or formal act of casting a vote, especially in an election.
Use 'poll' instead of 'vote' when emphasizing the counting or result of a vote, or the process of voting itself.
Use 'referendum' instead of 'vote' when referring to a direct vote by the electorate on a specific issue, often a policy or law.

senses.definition: use inefficiently or inappropriately

examples.text: waste heat

senses.definition: get rid of

examples.text: We waste the dirty water by channeling it into the sewer

senses.definition: spend extravagantly

examples.text: waste not, want not

senses.definition: cause extensive destruction or ruin utterly

examples.text: The enemy lay waste to the countryside after the invasion

senses.definition: spend thoughtlessly
spend thoughtlessly
run off as waste
get rid of (someone who may be a threat) by killing
lose vigor, health, or flesh, as through grief
cause to grow thin or weak
become physically weaker

connections.gloss: Use 'waste' for a broader, more general term that includes garbage and other discarded materials, especially in environmental or efficiency discussions.
Use when wasting small amounts of time or money on unimportant things.

senses.definition: a movement like that of a sudden occurrence or increase in a specified phenomenon

examples.text: a wave of settlers

senses.definition: something that rises rapidly

examples.text: a wave of emotion swept over him

senses.definition: a persistent and widespread unusual weather condition (especially of unusual temperatures)

examples.text: a heat wave

senses.definition: one of a series of ridges that moves across the surface of a liquid (especially across a large body of water)
one of a series of ridges that moves across the surface of a liquid (especially across a large body of water)
(physics) a movement up and down or back and forth
the act of signaling by a movement of the hand
a hairdo that creates undulations in the hair
an undulating curve
a member of the women's reserve of the United States Navy

connections.gloss: Use 'swell' for a long, smooth, unbroken wave, often in open water, emphasizing its gradual rise and fall.
Use 'surge' for a strong, sudden, and often forceful wave, emphasizing its power and momentum.

senses.definition: a shared orientation leading to mutual understanding

examples.text: they are on the same wavelength

senses.definition: the distance (measured in the direction of propagation) between two points in the same phase in consecutive cycles of a wave
the distance (measured in the direction of propagation) between two points in the same phase in consecutive cycles of a wave

connections.gloss: Use 'interval' instead of 'wavelength' when you want a more formal term for the spatial distance, but note it loses the specific phase reference.
Use 'span' to emphasize the full extent of a wave cycle in a more technical context.
Use 'extent' as a formal synonym for the measured length of a wave cycle, especially in written scientific descriptions.

senses.definition: an intricate network suggesting something that was formed by weaving or interweaving

examples.text: the trees cast a delicate web of shadows over the lawn

connections.gloss: Use 'web' for an intricate, often tangled set of connections, implying complexity or entanglement.
Use 'web' when referring to the World Wide Web specifically, or as a more vivid synonym for the internet.

senses.definition: Her meditation routine improved her overall well-being.
a contented state of being happy and healthy and prosperous

examples.text: Habits can impact our overall well-being.

connections.gloss: Use 'well-being' in formal contexts to emphasize health and happiness together, while 'upbeat' is more informal and often refers to temporary mood.

senses.definition: the cause or intention underlying an action or situation, especially in the phrase `the whys and wherefores'

examples.text: Why, then?

senses.definition: the cause or intention underlying an action or situation, especially in the phrase `the whys and wherefores'
The boat was pulled onto the trailer with a winch.
lifting device consisting of a horizontal cylinder turned by a crank on which a cable or rope winds

examples.text: The five-and-a-half-meter-diameter balloon is tethered with a winch cable to an airport pickup truck.

senses.definition: A site where work occurs; usually used in reference to construction work.

examples.text: Tom was supervising workers at the worksite.

senses.definition: All safety regulations must be followed at the construction worksite.
give or supply

examples.text: The land yields abundant crops.

senses.definition: be the cause or source of
be the cause or source of
end resistance, as under pressure or force
give over
give in, as to influence or pressure
move in order to make room for someone for something
cause to happen or be responsible for
be willing to concede
be fatally overwhelmed
bring in
be flexible under stress of physical force
cease opposition
consent reluctantly

connections.gloss: Use 'yield' when referring to the return from an investment or productive activity.
Use 'yield' for passive income from investments, like interest or dividends.
Use 'yield' when the profit or result comes from an asset or resource over time, often passive income.
Use 'yield' in agricultural or statistical contexts to emphasize quantity or output rather than the act of gathering.
Use 'yield' when something produces a result or outcome, often as a natural or expected consequence.
Use 'furnish' in formal or written contexts to mean 'provide' or 'supply' something needed; 'yield' often implies natural production or result.
Use 'yield' for measurable physical or agricultural output, especially from a process or land.
Use 'yield' to emphasize the amount or quantity produced, especially in technical or statistical contexts.
